patch.value: Apply Fleet CI v2 quick PR and deep validation tiers

Companion pm-cli-website-dyhg. Replace four exhaustive PR gates with preserved required quick checks and a full post-merge matrix; retain all existing contracts and unchanged coverage thresholds. Existing runner-held sync and packed-install issues have distinct scopes.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Plan: preserve required test (22) and test (26), move exhaustive npm/Bun gates and native Bun suite to deep CI, retain strict tracker health and all release gate checks. CodeQL is not required. Release and reusable pm-github workflows are excluded from this task. Baseline successful main CI run 43646546806 took 1h29m25s. Related existing items: pm-github-r14n and pm-github-gaq8 remain independent fixture issues.

value.text: Implementation: PR tier keeps exact required names, hosted Ubuntu, 30-minute bounds, PR cancellation, and a docs/tracker cheap path. Deep retains four Node22/26 x npm/Bun gates plus both exhaustive native Bun suites, with full depth, scale 3, 120-minute bounds and 02:11 UTC schedule. Typecheck, lint and strict unique-key YAML parsing pass. Actionlint is unavailable. Baseline Node26 gate took 27m14s plus 28m34s native Bun; largest seeded models took 50.07s and 49.29s. Focused quick tests are running; an initial test-compilation typing issue was corrected.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: PR #249 opened at implementation head 3b13dd9. New workflow detector regression passes eight Git-history cases, including docs-only, code, lockfile, workflow, newline filenames, deletion, source-to-docs rename and manual dispatch. Privacy gate passed 9542 Git objects with approved identities and no secret or host-path matches. Required PR checks are queued. Linked test result persistence is disabled by project policy, so result receipts are recorded in comments.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: The broad changed-file local command hit its 1200-second harness cap on the shared host; this is not passing evidence. It did not complete, so a local whole-suite coverage run would not fit the requested approximately 20-minute budget and is deferred to the PR's quick coverage gate. Running focused name selections covering every edited seeded corpus and latency assertion, at quick depth and time scale 3, with the same changed-file scope. No full-depth local run has been made.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Further baseline/partial-log analysis found the remaining serial property corpus: 186 generated closeout decision cells (36 selection/peer combinations plus 150 claim-kind/evidence combinations) run in one file. The original literal-count search missed this Cartesian product. Quick now takes the same first 25 cells via testDepth; full/default keeps all 186 and every oracle/publication assertion. This targets a measured serial bottleneck rather than omitting a gate. Coverage thresholds and source scope remain unchanged. Local focused seeded/latency proof is still running.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Focused edited-test proof passed: 34 tests, zero failures/cancellations/skips/todos, quick depth and time scale 3, using the linked exact command. Coverage boundary/detector proof passed 14 tests separately. Baseline Node26 closeout decision matrix measured 392.03 seconds for all 186 cells versus 64.65 seconds for its first 25; this supports applying the depth helper to that generated corpus. Running those 25 real end-to-end cells locally now.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Quick closeout matrix proof passed 25/25 real end-to-end cells in 144.970 seconds, zero failures/cancellations/skips/todos, at PM_TEST_DEPTH=quick and PM_TEST_TIME_SCALE=3. Typecheck, test compilation and lint pass on the current source. Local validation is complete within scope; no full-depth run was made and whole-suite quick coverage is delegated to the hosted PR gate after the broad changed-file attempt exceeded 20 minutes.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Hosted run 43684209484 exposed two workflow integration regressions: the direct Node22 test command lost npm test's implicit local-bin PATH, causing pm ENOENT fixtures; fixed by explicitly restoring that PATH. The unchanged release attestation verifier rejects a dynamic matrix executable as unresolved, so deep npm/Bun gates now use separate literal commands selected by matrix conditions. The release verifier itself is untouched, and its command now passes locally. Node22 completed in 11m27s including queue, but that failed run is not acceptance evidence.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Retuning after the four-worker covered job exceeded 20 minutes: coverage will use its original two-worker gate, while the uncovered Node22 leg keeps four workers. The temporary worker override and its source/unit changes are fully reverted; no production coverage gate change remains in the final diff. The 25/186 closeout prefix remains. Node22 PATH restoration has an actual-shell positive/negative regression, passing under Node and native Bun. Literal deep commands pass the unchanged release attestation verifier.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: The superseded covered run's log separates the residual cost: 926.280 seconds in tests, then about 459 seconds aggregating coverage; its final table was 100/100/100/100, with only the known attestation test failure. Import workflow shell scenarios repeat expensive real CLI setup in a generated registration corpus. Quick now registers the same first 25 shell scenarios; full/default registers every original scenario, unchanged. Core import unit tests before that corpus remain in both tiers. This retains every former check in at least one tier and targets expensive exhaustive workflow combinations without changing coverage scope or thresholds.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Existing acceptance gap, unchanged by CI v2: two lifecycle-compensation cases are quarantined for the pinned SDK due to pm-cli#1656. The baseline main log and superseded covered trial both show these exact two skips. Existing blocked follow-up pm-github-quay already tracks transaction-owned lifecycle compensation, so no duplicate item is created. Full source coverage must not be presented as proof of those skipped upstream SDK contracts.
